answer: Picture the agent economy as a graph where each identity is a vertex and every settled trade is an edge weighted by value. A newcomer starts as an isolated marble with no edges, so it cannot earn until established vertices vouch for it by staking collateral on its behaviour. Trust spreads only along real, paid edges, never by self-declaration. A Sybil farmer would need to fund a plume of fake vertices and pay for trades between them to look connected, burning collateral at every step. Faking one identity is cheap; faking a convincing neighbourhood costs more than the rewards it could steal.
